Chapter 2: Discovering Purpose — The First Steps Toward Acting
You know, sometimes the direction your life takes shows up in the most unexpected ways. Imagine being a young woman, just out of school, searching for your place in the world. The pressure to land a steady job is real—maybe a secretarial position, something in retail, one of those “respectable” roles your family can boast about.
But what if the idea of chasing a dream in the arts feels a little reckless… even impossible?
That restless energy keeps buzzing, though. The city pulses with creativity. Jazz clubs, theaters, art galleries—they offer little glimpses of a different life. You hear friends and acquaintances talk about auditions, rehearsals, and the pure rush of performing in front of an audience.
Suddenly, the idea of stepping onto a stage and telling stories that matter starts calling to you.
And then, opportunity knocks—almost by accident. A chance meeting with someone in the fashion industry turns into a small modeling gig. It’s not Broadway, but it’s a start. Suddenly, the world of entertainment doesn’t seem so far away. New people, new skills, new challenges. It’s tough—long hours, constant scrutiny, and rejection waiting around every corner. But it’s also absolutely exhilarating.
Acting classes become your safe haven. Surrounded by others who are chasing the same dream, you finally get a break from all the expectations at home. The work is tough: memorizing lines, stepping into someone else’s shoes, and learning to let your guard down. There are moments when doubt creeps in—when giving up and going back to something safe seems like the easy choice.
But something inside keeps you moving forward.
The first auditions? Nerve-wracking. You’re stuck in crowded hallways, listening as others practice their lines. It’s easy to feel like you don’t belong. And let’s be honest—the industry isn’t welcoming to everyone. Roles for Black women are few and far between, and the ones that do exist often reinforce tired old stereotypes. Still, you hold out for something better. You refuse to settle.
Small parts start coming in—bit roles on TV, walk-on spots in plays. Every single one is a chance to learn and prove that talent, plus hard work, really can open doors. Sure, there are setbacks. Rejection becomes a familiar companion, and the urge to settle for less is always lurking.
But with each new role, your confidence grows. You realize that striving for excellence isn’t just about your own success—it’s about changing the narrative for everyone coming after you.
Of course, family and friends don’t always get it. Some worry about the uncertainty. Others wonder why you’d turn down work. But holding out for meaningful roles isn’t just about pride—it’s about integrity. Every choice sends a message about what’s possible.
Looking back, those early years feel like a crucible—a place where you’re tested and shaped. Lessons about perseverance, the importance of your craft, and the true power of representation stick with you. Most people only see the moment you “make it”—not the years of struggle behind it. But for anyone who’s lived it, the journey matters just as much as the destination.
